question.problem: Let $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}9 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\},$ where ${c}_{1}=3{b}_{1}-2{b}_{2}$ and ${c}_{2}=-{b}_{2}?$
question.worked_solution:
We are given that

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}=3{b}_{1}-2{b}_{2} \\ {c}_{2}=-{b}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we express the $b$'s in terms of $c$'s. From the second equation, we get 

$$
{b}_{2}=-{c}_{2}.
$$

Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{c}_{1}=3{b}_{1}-2(-{c}_{2})\,⟹\,{b}_{1}=\frac{{c}_{1}-2{c}_{2}}{3}.
$$

Since $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}9 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$, we can write the vector $x$ as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =9{b}_{1}+2{b}_{2} \\  & =9(\frac{{c}_{1}-2{c}_{2}}{3})+2(-{c}_{2}) \\  & =3{c}_{1}-6{c}_{2}-2{c}_{2} \\  & =3{c}_{1}-8{c}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -8\end{aligned}].$
